_why: The brand lock. Decided BEFORE any frame exists, then never broken inside the piece. apple_audit.py enforces every field. To the audience, a rule followed everywhere reads as intention.
name: <brand> — <video type>
_palette_rule: Exactly 3. bg = the field, ink = type and product edges, accent = ONE thing per shot (a highlight, never a wash). Alpha variants of these are fine. Anything else goes in extra_allowed with a reason, or it doesn't go in.

type._rule: One family. Two weights. Headlines tight (-0.02em), body normal. SF Pro only inside Apple-UI mockups (licence).

background: Flat bg with at most one slow, low-contrast light falloff. It never moves faster than the product and never competes with it.

music._bands: 60–80 regal/cinematic · 90–110 smooth/effortless · 115–123 kinetic/sophisticated (a practitioner's convention, not measured — pick by the brand's feel, then stay in the band)

sfx._rule: Every SFX must help the viewer understand the product. After the mix: remove any that feels loud, decorative or out of place.

shots._rule: One shot = one idea. Key object centred. Each shot gets room to breathe. Transitions carry the eye (match, morph, push, mask, dissolve); a hard cut only when the cut IS the message.

banned: more than one accent per shot
